subject: Rotating exec coverage proposal + DST exception guidance for tri-regional demo
messages:
From: Oliver Zhang <oliver.z@peregrineanalytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Reyes <marta.reyes@peregrineanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Coordinating exec demo across US/EU/APAC (tight windows)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick follow-up after last week's discovery. We have three exec stakeholders who want to join the product demo: our CFO (US), CTO (Berlin), and Head of R&D (Singapore). They all want a short, focused walk-through and time for Q&A.

Reality: their local hours are tight and DST transitions this month make slots messy — US compasses fall back next weekend, and I believe EU already moved. Can your team propose a model that doesn't force one exec to dial in at 3am?

Our constraints:
- Prefer a single 45-minute slot (demo + 15 min buffer)
- Week of Nov 15 or Nov 22 preferred
- If we have to repeat for different regions, would prefer at most two runs

Would it help if you propose a rotating schedule (different weeks the execs take the worse slot) or an alternative?

Appreciate a pragmatic plan and a calendar stub if possible.

Thanks,
Oliver
Senior Dir, Analytics
Peregrine Analytics

P.S. Attaching our internal availability matrix (sent separately).

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Zhang <oliver.z@peregrineanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coordinating exec demo across US/EU/APAC (tight windows)

All, looped you in to help propose a defensible schedule for Peregrine. Key constraints: exec-level availability is short, they want one meeting if possible, and DST transitions differ across regions.

My suggested approach (draft):
1) Offer two candidate models to the customer:
   a) Single global slot at a UTC anchor that maximizes overlap (likely late US morning / late EU afternoon / early APAC evening).
   b) Rotating dual-run: two 45-minute runs on the same day — one optimized for Americas/EMEA and one for APAC — with an explicit rotation so the same execs aren't always inconvenienced.
2) Provide explicit DST exception notes in the calendar invite (time in all three timezones plus UTC).
3) Lock in exec-level slots (2-3 options) and send ICS with named fallback policy (auto-fallback to alternate model if any exec declines within 48 hours).

Kimberly/Rishi/Neha/Jonas: can you each reply with actual exec availability windows (local time) for week of Nov 15 and Nov 22? I'll summarize and send to Oliver + Marta.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T13:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Coordinating exec demo across US/EU/APAC (tight windows)

Vivek / team — quick availability and a DST note.

US exec (CFO) windows - Pacific time (local):
- Week of Nov 15: Mon/Wed/Thu 09:30–11:00 PT
- Week of Nov 22: Tue/Thu 10:00–11:30 PT

DST caveat: US clocks fall back Sunday Nov 7 (so local times shift). To avoid confusion, I'd anchor invites in UTC and list local equivalents in the invite copy.

I attached a small timezone-matrix I compiled showing the two candidate UTC anchors that give the best overlap: 16:00 UTC and 20:00 UTC. 16:00 UTC = 09:00 PT / 17:00 CET / 01:00 SGT (next day) — favors US/EU. 20:00 UTC = 13:00 PT / 21:00 CET / 05:00 SGT — favors APAC but is late for EU.

I'd recommend the rotating dual-run model: run A at 16:00 UTC (Americas/EMEA-friendly) + run B at 02:00 UTC (APAC-friendly) on alternating weeks, with the customer confirming which week they want which rotation. That way the Singapore exec only gets the late slot every other rotation.

Attaching: timezone-matrix.xlsx

-Kim
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T10:22:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Coordinating exec demo across US/EU/APAC (tight windows)

Vivek / team — adding EU exec constraints.

EU exec (CTO) windows — CET:
- Week of Nov 15: Tue/Thu 15:00–17:30 CET
- Week of Nov 22: Wed/Thu 09:30–11:00 CET

Note: EU switched back last weekend, so our local time is stable for Nov dates. 16:00 UTC corresponds to 17:00 CET — that is fine for our CTO on the week of Nov 15. If we do rotating runs, I'd prefer the EU exec not be scheduled for the 05:00 SGT-friendly slot except when they specifically opt in.

Proposed clarification to Oliver: offer two dates (Wed Nov 17 or Thu Nov 18) for the week of Nov 15, with the dual-run option on the same day (Run A 16:00 UTC; Run B 02:00 UTC next day) and an explicit rotation note. Wed/Thu are his preference.

— Jonas
Field CTO, EMEA

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T08:15:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Coordinating exec demo across US/EU/APAC (tight windows)

Team — I compiled availability into a single proposed schedule and added fallback rules. See below (times shown in UTC and local equivalents):

Proposed plan (final candidate):
- Option 1: Single global slot: 16:00 UTC on Wed Nov 17 (45 min) — pros: one meeting, highest overlap; cons: APAC exec joins ~01:00 SGT.
- Option 2: Rotating dual-run (recommended):
   • Run A: 16:00 UTC Wed Nov 17 (Americas/EMEA)
   • Run B: 02:00 UTC Thu Nov 18 (APAC-friendly)
   • Rotation policy: if Peregrine needs recurring demos, rotate which week contains the earlier/later run so the same exec isn't always late.

Fallbacks and escalation:
- If any named exec cannot attend either run, we will offer a 30-minute executive-only recap within 48 hours (private follow-up).
- If more than one exec declines, reschedule to alternate week window (Nov 22 options).

Attachments: proposed-rotating-schedule.ics, exec-availability.csv

If everyone signs off, I'll generate ICS invites (both runs) with times listed in UTC + the three local equivalents and send to Oliver for final pick.

-Rishi
Director, Sales Engineering

From: Oliver Zhang <oliver.z@peregrineanalytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Reyes <marta.reyes@peregrineanalytics.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T14:45:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Coordinating exec demo across US/EU/APAC (tight windows)

Vivek / Rishi / team — this looks great. We prefer Option 2 (rotating dual-run). Please send both ICS invites for Wed Nov 17 (16:00 UTC) and Thu Nov 18 (02:00 UTC) and label them clearly with local times + UTC. We'll ask our CFO and CTO to pick which run they will attend, and our Head of R&D will take the APAC-friendly run.

One ask: include in the invite text a short line explaining "Why two runs? rotation protects exec time across regions; if you prefer a single consolidated run, tell us and we'll re-evaluate." That transparency helps with internal approvals on our side.

Once we receive the ICS, we'll lock calendars.

Thanks — Oliver
Senior Dir, Analytics
Peregrine Analytics
